newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX index appears ready to break 3,900.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX index appears ready to break 3,900.

text.p: Germany's DAX index is poised to break the psychologically important level of 3,900 points by the end of the week as a firmer dollar and Wall Street gains give the share market fresh impulses, traders said on Thursday.

"The market still has a very friendly feeling and I think we have a relatively good chance of breaking 3,900 points by the weekend," said one Frankfurt trader. "The market is in good shape. We have sufficient volumes behind this advance."
The DAX index on Thursday ended bourse trade at another new record high, ending up 32.63 points at 3,887.39 points after setting a new all-time high at 3,894.66 points.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 20.77 points at 3,880.30 points in post-bourse activity.
Traders expected the market to remain steady ahead of the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. jobless data for May as the German market waits for the report's impact on U.S. financial markets.
But, barring a major surprise in the U.S. jobs report, the market should resume its climb and could face a test of the 4,000-point level in the DAX within two or three weeks.
Overnight Wall Street gains, where the Dow Jones index surged about one percent to 7,795.38 points, and the dollar trading above 1.75 marks were the main factors driving the DAX.
The higher dollar also underpinned export-sensitive shares, particularly in the chemical and automotive sectors.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG rose 57 marks to 1,402 marks, with traders citing the firmer dollar as a main factor.
BMW AG ended bourse trade up 33 marks at 1,457 marks after saying its U.S. car sales in June rose 12 percent.
Porsche, another top gainer in recent weeks, was up 165 marks at 2,675 marks. Brokerage house Lehman said this week it set a price target for Porsche at 3,600 marks.
Daimler-Benz AG ended up 30 pfennigs at 145.20 marks after also setting a new record high at 146.20 marks in IBIS.

Chemical shares, which were at the market forefront earlier in the week, were generally lower on profit-taking following recent sharp gains. But traders said the sector was still in vogue and that the uptrend would resume in the near-term.
Hoechst AG, which has risen more than 10 percent since June 25, ended bourse trade down 1.85 marks at 77.45 marks, while rival BASF AG ended down 20 pfennigs at 65.85 marks.
But Bayer AG ended up 40 pfennigs at 71.15 marks.
